enriched_description: Large nutlike seed with a smooth, glossy, hard shell in rich chestnut-brown coloration, typically 2-4 cm in diameter. The surface exhibits a distinctive pale circular scar (hilum) on one side, contrasting with the dark brown surrounding shell. The shape is roughly spherical with a slightly flattened base. The shell is taut and reflective with a warm, polished appearance. The seed is enclosed in a spiky green husk when fresh, which splits open to reveal the glossy nut.

Brightly colored fungus growing in intricately branched clusters resembling marine coral, typically 10-30 cm in height. The structure consists of numerous cylindrical branches arising from a common base, dividing repeatedly into finer tips. Coloration ranges from vivid yellow, orange, pink, to coral-red. The surface exhibits a smooth to slightly rough texture with a matte finish. Branch tips are pointed or slightly rounded. The overall form is an upright, bushy cluster with complex three-dimensional branching.

Mushroom with a characteristic umbrella-shaped cap (pileus) supported by a central cylindrical stem (stipe). The cap is convex to flat, 5-15 cm in diameter, with a smooth surface in white, brown, or tan coloration. The underside reveals radiating gills (lamellae) that are free from the stem, ranging from white to dark brown or black. The stem is smooth, white, and 5-10 cm tall, often with a ring (annulus) near the top. The overall form is the classic toadstool silhouette.

Fungus with a distinctive wrinkled, brain-like cap (pileus) in reddish-brown to dark brown coloration, typically 5-15 cm in diameter. The cap surface exhibits deep folds, ridges, and convolutions resembling cerebral cortex patterns. The cap is attached to a thick, white to pale tan stem that is often hollow and irregularly shaped. The overall form is irregular and asymmetrical with a saddle-shaped or lobed cap. Height ranges from 8-20 cm.

Distinctive fungus with a tall, phallic-shaped structure emerging from a white egg-like base (volva). The stem (receptaculum) is white to pale pink, 10-25 cm tall, with a spongy, porous texture. The cap (gleba) at the top is conical or bell-shaped, covered in a dark olive-brown to black slimy spore mass that emits a foul, carrion-like odor. The surface of the gleba is wet and glossy. The stem is hollow and fragile.

Fungus with a distinctive star-shaped outer layer surrounding a central spherical spore sac. The outer peridium splits into 4-12 pointed rays that curve outward and downward, forming a star pattern 5-15 cm in diameter. The rays are thick and leathery with a brown to grayish-brown coloration. The central spore sac is spherical, 1-3 cm in diameter, with a smooth, papery surface in pale gray to brown. A small opening (ostiole) at the top of the sac releases spores when disturbed.

Large polypore fungus forming a dense cluster of overlapping, fan-shaped caps resembling a hen's plumage, typically 30-60 cm in diameter. The individual caps are 3-10 cm wide with a greyish-brown upper surface exhibiting concentric zones of lighter and darker coloration. The surface is slightly hairy or smooth with a matte finish. The undersides show white to cream-colored pores. The caps arise from a common branching base at the foot of a tree. The overall form is a cascading, layered rosette.

Mushroom with a convex cap (pileus) 5-20 cm in diameter, supported by a thick, bulbous stem (stipe). The cap surface is smooth to slightly velvety in brown, tan, or reddish coloration. Unlike agarics, the underside features a spongy layer of tubes (pores) rather than gills, ranging from white to yellow to green. The stem is stout, often reticulated (net-like pattern), and 5-15 cm tall. The flesh is firm and may bruise blue when cut. Overall form is robust and substantial.

Elongated fruiting spike of a cereal plant, typically 15-30 cm in length, consisting of a central axis (rachis) bearing rows of tightly packed grains (kernels). The surface exhibits a textured pattern from the individual grain units, each enclosed in a papery husk (glume). Coloration ranges from golden-yellow to pale green depending on maturity. The ear is attached to a tall, slender stalk with long, narrow leaves. Silk threads (styles) may protrude from the tip in younger specimens.

Soft, thin, absorbent paper product wound into a cylindrical roll around a cardboard tube. The paper exhibits a white or off-white coloration with a slightly textured, embossed surface pattern (quilted or dotted). Individual sheets are perforated for easy tearing. The roll is typically 10-12 cm in diameter and 10 cm wide. The surface shows a matte, fibrous texture with visible paper fibers at close range. The cardboard core is visible at the center of the roll.
